title: The pre-mortem with tripwires
promise: Stress a plan before you commit to it: the ways it fails, the evidence for each, and the number that tells you to stop.
gives: A one-page risk register: ranked failure stories, each top one with a tripwire, an owner and a date.
clipLine: Each top risk gets a metric, a threshold, an owner and a date.
when: A plan is about to be approved and everyone in the room likes it.
You are writing a PRD and want the constraints before the scope.
A launch has a date and no stated condition for pulling it.
skip: The plan is one sentence. Write it down first.
You need a compliance or legal review. This raises questions for those teams. It does not answer them.
The decision is already made and nobody will act on a risk.

inputs.name: The plan
inputs.note: A PRD, a memo or half a page: what ships, to whom, and what it is meant to change.

inputs.name: What you already know
inputs.note: Research, numbers, past attempts. Risks are weighed against this.

inputs.name: What you can measure
inputs.note: The metrics you actually have, so tripwires use real ones.

outputs.name: premortem.html
outputs.note: The register: a likelihood and impact grid and one card per risk.

outputs.name: premortem.json
outputs.note: The risks as data. The PRD skill turns the top ones into constraints.

steps.title: Assume it failed
steps.body: Each risk is written as a short story dated six months after launch. Six areas are covered: users, behaviour, operations, money, rules and reputation, and build.

steps.title: Demand evidence for each story
steps.body: For every risk it states what you would expect to see if it were true, and whether your inputs support it, contradict it or say nothing.

steps.title: Rank by likelihood and impact
steps.body: Each is rated low, medium or high, with a reason. A risk with no supporting evidence is marked as a guess.

steps.title: Attach a tripwire to the top risks
steps.body: A metric you already have, a threshold, a date to check it and who checks.

steps.title: Say what would change the plan
steps.body: A mitigation that changes scope, and the cheapest test that would settle the risk before launch.

checks.name: Every top risk has a complete tripwire
checks.note: Metric, threshold, check date and owner are all required. A threshold with no number in it is rejected.

checks.name: Evidence is labelled
checks.note: Each risk is marked supported, contradicted or unknown, names the input it rests on, and says what you would expect to see if it were true.

checks.name: All six areas were considered
checks.note: An area with no risk has to say why.

checks.name: The list is short enough to act on
checks.note: Twelve risks at most, three to five with tripwires, and no more than five rated high on both likelihood and impact.

checks.name: Every risk is a story
checks.note: 25 to 90 words: who, doing what, and what follows. A one-line worry is rejected.

checks.name: Tripwires use metrics you have
checks.note: Check each metric exists in your dashboards today.

failures.title: A long list of plausible worries
failures.body: Models are good at generating risks. Twenty risks are as useful as none.
failures.catch: The output is capped and only the top ones get tripwires. If everything is rated high, ask it to rank again against your evidence.

failures.title: It cannot know your organisation
failures.body: The risk that kills most plans is internal: a dependency, a reorganisation, a team nobody asked.
failures.catch: Add those yourself in the review. The build area is where they belong.

failures.title: Tripwires nobody watches
failures.body: A threshold in a document is not a decision.
failures.catch: Each tripwire has an owner and a date. Put the date in a calendar before you close the file.

changelog.note: The checker now lists each tripwire's metric for the owner to confirm, warns on a relative threshold that is not labelled as a proposal, and names every high-impact risk left out of the top list. The instructions say how to choose check dates and how to tell the user about risks that have no metric. Found by the two test runs of 19 November.

tangelo.label: One-tap reorder, six months on
tangelo.note: Eleven failure stories across six areas. The top five carry tripwires, and six are marked as guesses.
tangelo.ask: Run a pre-mortem on the one-tap reorder plan.
tangelo.demoNote: The agent assumes the plan failed, writes how, and weighs each story against the research. The top risks get a tripwire. When it ends, click a risk to read it.

run.by: A fresh agent session, given only the skill folder and the plan. Nobody answered its questions.
run.note: It passed on the first run of the checker. The run changed the plan itself, and it listed sixteen gaps in the instructions. The ones that mattered are fixed in this version.

carousel.title: Start by assuming *it failed*
carousel.body: The date is six months after launch. The plan shipped, and it went badly.

carousel.title: Eleven ways it *went wrong*
carousel.body: Stories across six areas, placed by how likely each is and how much it would hurt.

carousel.title: Evidence, or *a guess*
carousel.body: Each story is weighed against the research. Six of the eleven have no evidence either way, and the page says so.

carousel.title: A tripwire has *a number, a date and a name*
carousel.body: The metric to watch, the line it must not cross, the day to look, and who looks.

carousel.title: Five dates *for the calendar*
carousel.body: The worst five risks, each with the day someone checks it.

larkspur.label: Team suggestions, six months on
larkspur.note: Ten failure stories across six areas. The top five carry tripwires, and three are marked as guesses.
larkspur.ask: Run a pre-mortem on the Team suggestions plan before we commit to it.
larkspur.demoNote: The agent assumes the plan to invite five people with one button has failed, writes ten ways it went wrong and weighs each against the teardown and the interviews. The worst five get a tripwire. When it ends, click a risk to read it.

run.by: A fresh agent session with only the skill folder and the inputs
run.note: It passed on the first run of the checker, and the run changed the plan. It also found that with no baseline to work from, the numbers in the tripwires are the agent's own proposals, and the skill should say so plainly.

vireo.label: Auto-assign, six months on
vireo.note: Ten failure stories across six areas. The top five carry tripwires, and three are marked as guesses.
vireo.ask: Run a pre-mortem on the Auto-assign plan before we commit to it.
vireo.demoNote: The agent assumes Auto-assign has failed, writes ten ways it went wrong and weighs each against the teardown and the interviews. The worst five get a tripwire, starting with a wrong recap that reaches an outside guest. When it ends, click a risk to read it.

run.by: A fresh agent session with only the skill folder and the inputs
run.note: It passed on the first run of the checker, and the run changed the plan. It also found that the risk with the biggest impact, legal blocking the send to guests, has no metric today, so it carries no tripwire and no date.
